question: The concept of 'sustainable development' was introduced by which one of the following reports?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Brundtland report.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **sustainable development** was popularized by the **Brundtland report, officially titled *Our Common Future*.**
 
• **Published in 1987 by the World Commission on Environment and Development** (WCED), the report emphasized the interconnection between economic growth, environmental sustainability, and social equity.
 
• **The report defined sustainable development as "development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs."**
 
• **It laid the groundwork for international environmental policies and discussions, influencing major conferences like the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro.**
 
• **The Brundtland report highlighted the need for global cooperation and integrated approaches to address environmental issues and promote sustainable practices.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Rio Declaration**: Adopted in 1992 at the Earth Summit, it outlines principles for sustainable development but does not introduce the concept itself.
 
• **Johannesburg Declaration**: Formulated during the World Summit on Sustainable Development in 2002, it builds upon the ideas presented in the Brundtland report but does not originate the concept.
 
• **Agenda 21**: A comprehensive plan of action for sustainable development established at the Earth Summit in 1992, it is a result of the Brundtland report's influence but is not the original source of the term.
 
• **World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED)**: Established by the United Nations in 1983, it aimed to address the growing issues of environment and development and promote sustainable practices globally.
 
• **Impact of the Brundtland Report**: The report has shaped international policies, development programs, and discussions on sustainability, influencing agendas in various sectors, including climate change and poverty reduction.
